body.estimand_functional: \(\theta_B\in[L(p_Q),U(p_Q)]=\left[\sum_xF_L\{H_x(p_Q)\}/M(p_Q),\sum_xF_U\{H_x(p_Q)\}/M(p_Q)\right]\), by the imported AcceptedSlateBenefit2026 sharp-endpoint theorem

sampling_model.design: For each \(n\), observe an independent sample \(O_{n1},\ldots,O_{nn}\) from the row law \(P_n\in\mathcal M\); rows may vary arbitrarily with \(n\).
sampling_model.units: The number of multinomial atoms \(|\mathcal J|\) is fixed, while their probabilities may vanish with \(n\).
sampling_model.treatment: The instrument and treatment are binary; the outcome has the fixed ordered support \(\mathcal Y\), and selection is observed.
sampling_model.overlap: The inferential class strengthens the inherited pointwise model only by fixed uniform bounds \(\epsilon\le P_n(Z=1\mid X=x)\le1-\epsilon\) and \(M(p_n)\ge m_*\); individual cells and cut gaps may vanish.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The empirical atom vector \(\widehat p_n\) is the sole first-stage estimator. Algebraic division is totalized by \(u\oslash0=0\), the endpoint center uses \(\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(\widehat p_n)=(0,1)\) at zero aggregate empirical mass, and \(C_n=\mathbb R^2\) when that fallback is invoked or the legal base set is empty. The common Gaussian draw is realized through the principal covariance square root, and its measurable critical value uses the lower-quantile convention. No support screening, variance floor, or deterministic calibration guard is used.

body.tldr: The accepted sharp-identification theorem supplies \(\Theta_I(p)=[L(p),U(p)]\) for the survivor-complier probability of benefit. The present result proves that the explicit nearby-legal-base envelope and its common-Gaussian max-norm rectangle cover the endpoint vector uniformly over every legal triangular array under only fixed instrument overlap and \(M(p)\ge m_*\), even when individual covariate or survivor cells, cut gaps, and both endpoint variances vanish. A finite latent-simplex probe construction turns every operative capacity face into a derivative at a positive-cell legal base. It yields either exact local flatness or probe standard deviation at least a constant times \(a_n\) times coefficient oscillation; this makes the multinomial and plug-in covariance errors relatively negligible because \(\sqrt n a_n\to\infty\). Separated regular faces retain exact oracle Gaussian calibration, while the established root-\(n\) width and \(K=4\) diagnostics remain unchanged.

project_justification.gap: The accepted parent settles sharp identification for the finite ordered survivor-complier benefit interval. Existing inference results either impose fixed-law differentiability, start from supplied asymptotically linear endpoint or standardized moment representations, or require geometric and positive-variance regularity that excludes changing support and a jointly collapsing endpoint scale.
project_justification.niche: The finite binary-instrument model permits exact capacity geometry and multinomial coupling, yet legality of nearby observed laws is more restrictive than ambient perturbation of a probability vector. This creates a tractable model-specific route to uniform inference at zero cells and tied extrema.
project_justification.fill: The total legal-base envelope retains every nearby support and cut face and uses one Gaussian draw for both endpoints. Finite response-type transfers now prove the legal face lift, exact segment domination, and a flatness-or-traction dichotomy; scale-free anti-concentration then transfers the lower conditional critical value uniformly, including a collapsing endpoint scale.

body.related_work: The accepted CausalSmith survivor-complier benefit result supplies the exact sharp endpoint formula and full-law sharpness; identification is imported rather than reproved. Angrist, Imbens, and Rubin (1996) support conditional instrument randomization, treatment consistency, and no defiers, while Dong and Heiler (2026) support treatment-mediated selection and outcome consistency together with covariate-specific weak selection monotonicity. The fixed \(\epsilon\) overlap bound and fixed \(m_*\) denominator floor are uniform-class strengthenings here. Fang and Santos (2019) and Hong and Li (2018) explain derivative-resampling methods, but their generic results do not construct the required nearby legal observed laws. Frandsen and Pond (2025) begin from asymptotically normal bound estimators; Imai and Okamoto (2026) require supplied uniformly asymptotically linear endpoints and nonvanishing standard deviations; Andrews and Guggenberger (2009) work with standardized moment-inequality statistics of positive component variance. The finite latent-simplex legalization proved here is model-specific and distinct from those premises. Vijaykumar (2026), Proposition 4, supplies the scale-free density bound for the unsigned Gaussian maximum used after the probe traction inequality; it does not supply that legal geometry or the relative multinomial comparison.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The uniform proof is asymptotic and uses fixed finite \(K\) and \(\mathcal X\), fixed overlap \(\epsilon\), fixed aggregate floor \(m_*\), and \(\sqrt n a_n\to\infty\). It supplies no finite-sample coverage error constant and no polynomial-time claim for computing the legal-base supremum. Zero-cell algebraic derivatives remain total scaffolding only: the proof's load-bearing probe rows are all realized at positive-cell legal bases. If the aggregate empirical mass is zero or the random legal base set is empty, the stated full-plane fallback remains part of the procedure.
body.honest_scope: Sharp identification is imported from the accepted parent and is not a contribution of this note. The contribution is uniform joint inference for that fixed endpoint map under the inherited finite binary-instrument model, strengthened only by fixed instrument overlap and a fixed aggregate survivor-complier mass floor. No lower bound is imposed on an individual covariate cell, survivor cell, active-cut gap, or endpoint variance, and no support screen, variance floor, endpoint-wise Bonferroni device, or deterministic calibration guard is introduced. Exact oracle behavior is asserted separately only on fixed separated regular faces; the uniform theorem requires honesty, not exactness, on tied or degenerating faces.
body.interpretation: The rectangle is a simultaneous confidence set for the sharp endpoint pair \(\Phi(p_n)=(L(p_n),U(p_n))\), not a redefinition of the causal probability \(\theta_B\). Because the imported identification theorem gives \(\Theta_I(p_n)=[L(p_n),U(p_n)]\), covering both endpoints gives one honest inferential statement about the entire sharp benefit interval. The common draw preserves endpoint dependence and is generally narrower than coordinatewise Bonferroni calibration on regular faces.
